subject: Math
prompt:
[Figure 1]

The circle shown has center $M$, circumference $84\pi$, and diameters $AC$ and $BD$. The length of arc $DA$ is twice the length of arc $AB$. What is the length of arc $BC$?
explanation: Choice C is correct. Since $\overline{AC}$ and $\overline{BD}$ are diameters of the circle, $\overline{MA}$, $\overline{MB}$, $\overline{MC}$, and $\overline{MD}$ are radii and are therefore congruent. Since $\angle DMA$ and $\angle BMC$ are vertical angles, they are congruent, so arcs $DA$ and $BC$ are congruent. Similarly, $\angle AMB$ and $\angle CMD$ are vertical angles, so arcs $AB$ and $CD$ are congruent. Let $x$ represent the length of arc $AB$; then arc $CD$ also has length $x$. It is given that the length of arc $DA$ is twice the length of arc $AB$, so arc $DA$ has length $2x$, and by congruence arc $BC$ also has length $2x$. The four arcs together form the full circumference, so $x + x + 2x + 2x = 84\pi$, which gives $6x = 84\pi$, and therefore $x = 14\pi$. The length of arc $BC$ is $2(14\pi) = 28\pi$.
